name: Zhujiang New Town (Tianhe)
tagline: Glass towers, metro lines and the expat centre of gravity
description: Zhujiang New Town is Guangzhou's purpose-built CBD, a grid of glass office towers around a landscaped central axis running from the opera house to the Canton Tower. Ground floors hold international supermarkets, specialty coffee and serviced apartments. Nearly every corporate expat, consulate worker and well-paid remote worker in the city lives within a few blocks.
bestFor: Nomads who want English-friendly services, fast fibre and a metro interchange under the building.
pros: Best internet and newest serviced apartments in the city
Metro lines 3 and 5 plus APM meet here
Dense cluster of cafes, gyms and international groceries
cons: Sterile at street level, feels empty after office hours
Line 3 at rush hour is genuinely crushing

name: Yuexiu
tagline: The old city core with parks and street food
description: Yuexiu is historic Guangzhou: Beijing Road pedestrian street, Yuexiu Park with the Five Rams statue, tree-shaded avenues of 1950s blocks and wet markets on every second corner. It is dense, walkable and utterly Chinese, with cheap noodle shops and dim sum houses instead of brunch spots. Older local families and students make up most residents.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk everywhere and eat local food rather than sit in an expat bubble.
pros: Genuinely walkable with parks and markets everywhere
Cheap authentic food, dim sum from around $3
Central metro access to the whole city
cons: Older apartments with thin walls and weak air conditioning
Very little English spoken in shops
Crowded pavements and constant scooter traffic

name: Liwan (Xiguan and Shamian)
tagline: Arcade houses, canals and colonial Shamian Island
description: Liwan holds the prettiest old Guangzhou: the qilou arcade shophouses of Shangxiajiu, the willow-lined Litchi Bay canals and Shamian Island, a tiny leafy former concession of European villas closed to through traffic. Rents are moderate and the streets are full of tea houses and herbal soup shops. It suits people who value character over convenience.
bestFor: Slow travellers and photographers who want the most characterful streets in the city.
pros: Most attractive historic streetscape in Guangzhou
Shamian Island is quiet, green and car-free
Good value rents for a central district
cons: Shangxiajiu is packed with tourists at weekends
Fewer coworking spaces and modern buildings
Longer metro rides to the CBD side of town

name: Haizhu (Party Pier and Chigang)
tagline: Riverside living opposite the Canton Tower
description: Haizhu sits on the island south of the Pearl River, and its northern strip around Party Pier and Chigang has riverside walkways, converted warehouse bars and views straight across to the Canton Tower. Behind the waterfront are ordinary residential towers and the huge Zhongda fabric market. It is calmer than Tianhe but one metro stop away.
bestFor: Nomads who want CBD access at a discount plus a river to run along.
pros: Cheaper than Tianhe but a single metro stop from it
Long riverside promenade for running and evening walks
Good craft beer and warehouse bar scene at Party Pier
cons: Traffic funnels onto a few bridges and jams badly
Riverside bar strip gets loud on weekend nights
Humidity feels worse right by the water in summer

name: Baiyun
description: Baiyun is the large district north of the old city, named for Baiyun Mountain, whose forested trails are the best hiking within the city limits. Housing is plentiful, plain and cheap, ranging from urban villages to newer mid-rise blocks near Baiyun New Town. Migrant workers, students and budget-minded residents fill it rather than expats.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads on a tight budget who do not mind a commute for a much lower rent.
pros: Rents can be half of Tianhe for similar space
Baiyun Mountain hiking trails on the doorstep
Very cheap street food and local markets
cons: 30 to 45 minutes on the metro to the CBD
Almost no English and few expat services
Uneven building quality, check internet before signing
